question: Can a model trained on some sites forecast next-day NASA POWER solar irradiance at geographically unseen sites, and does a compact learned model beat persistence and a simple linear baseline under that shift?
missing_policy: Replace -999 with NaN; linearly interpolate interior gaps of <=3 days within a site; drop any sample whose history window or target still has NaN. No imputation across sites.
aggregation: Per-site metrics are reported first; the headline number is the unweighted mean across sites.

baselines.persistence: prediction for day t+1 = observed target on day t

ridge.description: Ridge regression on flattened 7-day history of target + covariates + sin/cos day-of-year, standardised with train-site statistics

model_selection_rule: Hyperparameters and any later model/feature/stopping choice are selected ONLY by lowest mean MAE on the validation sites. Held-out sites are never used for fitting, scaling, tuning, feature selection or early stopping. Ties go to the simpler model.
freeze_note: Do not edit this file after the first baseline commit. Any change must be a new contract_version with a documented reason.
